findings.title: Migration can fail immediately if the legacy index was already removed
findings.evidence: The upgrade path executes an unconditional index drop before any table cleanup, so any database state where that index is absent will abort the migration at this statement and prevent the rest of the upgrade from running.
findings.recommendation: Make the migration idempotent for supported upgrade states, for example by using IF EXISTS or by checking schema metadata before dropping the index, so reruns and partially migrated databases do not fail.

findings.title: Unconditional table drop permanently deletes all legacy user data
findings.evidence: The migration now executes a direct table drop with no backup, copy, or downgrade logic visible in the diff, which irreversibly removes every row in that table as soon as upgrade runs.
findings.recommendation: Only drop the table after a verified data migration and add a reversible or staged cleanup path, such as renaming first, archiving data, or guarding the drop behind explicit confirmation that the table is no longer needed.
